description: Predeclared long-FFT research experiments, not a declaration of current kernel support.

rules: Reject unsupported shapes before allocation; do not silently pad or substitute another transform.
All correctness trials must pass; retain failures, losing configurations and every raw trial.
Match transform, precision, direction, normalization, placement and timing scope across baselines.
Budget input, output, workspace, host staging and numerical references before launching.
Record hardware, software, revision, clocks, warmup, repeat and selected mapping for every run.
Freeze workload splits and the candidate search budget before collecting publication results.

experiments.title: Legal length and memory envelope
experiments.hypothesis: Segmented execution extends C2C beyond the single-AIV UB limit without hiding boundary storage costs.
baselines: Current single-AIV implementation: unsupported reference, never timed as a long-FFT baseline
Available CANN/native long C2C with matched semantics
acceptance: 65536 and all declared supported lengths pass every trial
Unsupported or memory-infeasible points produce explicit reasons
No hidden truncation or padding

experiments.title: Single-transform and low-batch latency
experiments.hypothesis: Long FFT decomposition provides competitive latency while exposing setup and launch overhead separately.
baselines: Ascend FFT fixed legal segmented mapping
Ascend FFT model-selected mapping
Ascend FFT measured-search mapping
Available CANN/native long C2C with matched semantics
acceptance: All 24 semantic shapes reported including failures and regressions
Model and measured-search results are separately identified
No universal speedup requirement is imposed

experiments.title: Equal total points across FFT lengths
experiments.hypothesis: At equal total work, variation with FFT length reveals dependency, boundary and steady-state costs rather than merely data volume.
baselines: Ascend FFT fixed legal segmented mapping
Ascend FFT model-selected mapping
Ascend FFT measured-search mapping
Available CANN/native long C2C with matched semantics
acceptance: Each row satisfies N times batch equals its declared total_points
Each equal-work series reports all eight lengths
Large-memory cases are explicitly skipped when budget is insufficient

experiments.title: Batch saturation and mapping breakpoints
experiments.hypothesis: Resident subgraph reuse amortizes fixed overhead but steady-state throughput depends on role balance and hardware-resource breakpoints.
experiments.hardware_note: 48D +/- 1 batches are provisional Ascend910_9382 controls for D=1..4. Recompute for the local AIV count and legal long-FFT mappings.
baselines: Ascend FFT fixed legal segmented mapping
Ascend FFT model-selected mapping
Available CANN/native long C2C with matched semantics
acceptance: 65536 has all declared batch values
Mapping changes and tails are recorded rather than smoothed away
Hardware-dependent breakpoints are not claimed universal

experiments.title: Architecture and processing-unit ablations
experiments.hypothesis: Residence, overlap and online reorder provide separable benefits when arithmetic cores and legal resource envelopes are controlled.
baselines: Within-pair control implementation; unavailable controls are reported as not implemented
acceptance: Both pair members pass identical correctness contracts
Infeasible exact pairs are reported rather than replaced silently
Resource tradeoffs are disclosed; overlap is measured, not inferred from naming

experiments.title: Long-length numerical correctness
experiments.hypothesis: Reordered and segmented butterflies preserve FFT semantics with acceptable FP32 error as dependency depth grows.
baselines: Host higher-precision FFT reference
Analytical output for zero, impulse, constant and single-tone inputs
acceptance: Every input/seed/trial must pass the predeclared tolerance policy
Near-zero outputs use an absolute-error guard
Small-batch tests check all rows; larger tests declare coverage explicitly
Inverse round-trip is added only after an inverse implementation exists

experiments.title: Long-convolution and spectral workload proxies
experiments.hypothesis: Benefits persist on predeclared application-shaped workloads rather than only a favorable synthetic grid.

applications.scope: Forward C2C proxy only; full convolution requires inverse and pointwise multiplication
Dense one-dimensional spectral transform, not a multidimensional application

baselines: Available CANN/native long C2C with matched semantics
Host numerical reference; not a device-performance baseline
acceptance: Proxy results are labeled as proxies, not complete application speedups
No unsupported R2C, inverse or 2D capability is implied
All predeclared points including losing points are published

experiments.title: Traffic, overlap and model attribution
experiments.hypothesis: Parameterized compute, traffic, synchronization and fill/drain terms explain long-FFT performance across held-out lengths and batches.
controlled_variables: Same verified binary and mapping as timing run
baselines: Fixed legal mapping
Model-selected mapping
Measured-search oracle under a declared finite candidate budget
acceptance: 65536 is profiled at low and high batch
Calibration and held-out semantic keys do not overlap
Predicted costs and model uncertainty are reported
Profiler timings are not substituted for unprofiled latency measurements
Unavailable counters are marked unavailable, not zero
